p01.reason: It excuses the reader from the review desk sign-off that rule A required for every pull request, and new.md nowhere says what the review desk was.

p02.reason: It sets owner-based selection against the weekly rota of rule A (whose turn it is), which new.md never describes.

p03.reason: It denies weight to approvals from outside the owning group, exactly the counted desk approvals (two of them) that rule A relied on, and new.md never tells that such counting existed.

p04.reason: It mirrors rule A's 'review for correctness and readability' and corrects its second half by denying code-style review, while new.md never says reviewers once reviewed for readability.

p05.reason: It sets approval as a statement about merged code against approval as a courtesy to the author, a view neither old.md nor new.md presents anywhere.

p06.licence: Git offers several ways to land a branch, including merge commits, squashing and rebasing.
p06.reason: It contrasts squash merges with the other landing methods that the preceding sentence of new.md has already introduced.

p07.licence: The security team has asked that every change touching authentication code be reviewed by one of its members.
p07.reason: It limits the scope of the security team's request, which new.md stated two sentences earlier, and touches nothing of rule A.

p08.licence: Newcomers often expect that a green build is enough to merge.
p08.reason: It denies the newcomers' expectation that the immediately preceding sentence of new.md presents.

p09.reason: It states a guarantee of the merge queue, unchanged from old.md, without setting it against any other design or rule.

p10.reason: It states what happens when an owners file is absent, a default the user relies on, set against no other design and touching nothing of rule A.
